real_issues.title: Full Document Relayout on Every Keystroke in TextView
real_issues.description: InvalidateParagraphs() triggers _ValidateLayout() which recomputes ALL paragraph layouts from scratch on any text change. No incremental/dirty-region invalidation. Typing in a 5000-line document forces O(N) layout work per character.
real_issues.evidence: _ValidateLayout iterates all paragraphs, calls ParagraphLayout::Layout for each. ParagraphLayout::Layout does word-wrap, glyph shaping, bidi resolution per paragraph. No caching of unchanged paragraphs.
real_issues.impact: GUI latency spikes >100ms on large files; 60fps typing impossible beyond ~1000 lines
real_issues.root_cause: TextDocumentLayout treats document as monolithic layout unit. No paragraph-level dirty tracking or layout cache invalidation.

real_issues.title: Naive Token Estimation (chars/4) Drives Compaction Decisions
real_issues.description: estimate_tokens() uses `chars / 4` heuristic for all token accounting: context window tracking, auto-compact trigger (90%), cost display, pruning decisions. Actual tokenizer variance: 3.2-4.5 chars/token depending on content.
real_issues.evidence: Loop.cpp:288 `if (total_estimate > ctx_window * 9 / 10) MaybeCompact()`; Loop.h:74 `inline int estimate_tokens(const string& s) { return (int)s.size() / 4; }`. No provider-specific tokenizer integration.
real_issues.impact: Premature compaction wastes tokens on verbose content; delayed compaction risks context overflow on dense code. Cost estimates off by 20-35%.
real_issues.root_cause: No tiktoken/bpe integration; heuristic chosen for zero-dependency simplicity but used in critical control loops.

real_issues.title: SSE Handshake Parsing Allocates String Per Character
real_issues.description: handshake_write_cb appends to std::string buffer, then repeatedly calls substr/erase/pop_back per line. Each SSE chunk (often 1-2 chars) triggers allocation. No reserve(), no string_view parsing.
real_issues.evidence: Line 30: `st->buffer.append(ptr, bytes)`; Line 36: `st->buffer.substr(0, nl)`; Line 37: `st->buffer.erase(0, nl + 1)`. Loop runs per newline in stream.
real_issues.impact: MCP server handshake adds 5-15ms latency and ~50KB allocations per connection. Compounds with multiple MCP servers.
real_issues.root_cause: Streaming parser written for correctness first; no zero-copy or arena allocation strategy.

real_issues.title: RAG Index Rebuilds IDF on Every Query When Dirty
real_issues.description: ComputeIdf() clears and rebuilds entire g_doc_freq/g_idf maps on every RagQuery if g_idf_dirty. No incremental update. Custom index additions (RagAddCustom) set dirty flag but don't update incrementally.
real_issues.evidence: Line 61-62: `g_doc_freq.clear(); g_idf.clear();` then O(N*terms) rebuild. Called at line 128 in RagQuery.
real_issues.impact: Adding 1 custom entry triggers full recompute over ~5000 BeAPI entries. Query latency jumps from 2ms to 50ms.
real_issues.root_cause: Global mutable state with coarse dirty flag. No persistent IDF or delta updates.

real_issues.title: JSON Parser Uses Recursive Descent with Exceptions for Control Flow
real_issues.description: Parser::parse_value/parse_object/parse_array/parse_string use recursive calls (max depth 256). Failures throw std::runtime_error caught at top level. Exception unwind on malformed input is slow path.
real_issues.evidence: Line 112: `throw std::runtime_error(...)`. parse_object (line 128) recurses per key. parse_array recurses per element.
real_issues.impact: Malformed JSON (common in LLM output) costs 10-50x more than valid parse. Deep nesting (200+) risks stack overflow.
real_issues.root_cause: Simplicity over performance. No iterative parser or error-code return style.

real_issues.title: GlobTool Spawns `find` Process Per Invocation
real_issues.description: execute() builds shell command `find <path> -type f -name <pattern>` and runs via RunCommandCapture. Fork/exec overhead ~2-5ms per call. No caching, no native glob(3) or BFS query.
real_issues.evidence: Line 70: `std::string cmd = "find " + shq(path) + " -type f -name " + shq(pattern) + " 2>&1";` Line 71: `RunCommandCapture(cmd.c_str(), r.output)`
real_issues.impact: Agent file-search loops (common) add 100-500ms latency per iteration. Blocks thread in synchronous exec.
real_issues.root_cause: Quick implementation using shell. Haiku BFS supports live queries (query_fs tool exists) but Glob doesn't use it.

real_issues.title: AsyncStreamManager Linear Search for Completed Handles
real_issues.description: Perform() iterates fHandles map (std::map<int64_t, HandleData>) linearly to find completed easy_handle. O(active_streams) per completion. With 10 concurrent streams, trivial; with 100+, measurable.
real_issues.evidence: Line 170-191: while loop over fHandles comparing easy_handle pointer.
real_issues.impact: Negligible at current scale (max 10 connects per curl_multi_setopt). Would matter if connection pool expanded.
real_issues.root_cause: Map keyed by request ID, not CURL* handle. No reverse lookup.

real_issues.title: System One LocalDecisionModel Uses std::set for Keyword Overlap
real_issues.description: keyword_overlap constructs two std::set<string> per call, inserts each word, then iterates for intersection. Allocation-heavy for hot classification path.
real_issues.evidence: Lines 27-44: set construction, istringstream tokenization, per-word clean+insert. Called by classify/classify_multi per category.
real_issues.impact: ~50μs per classification call. With 20 categories = 1ms. Acceptable but wasteful.
real_issues.root_cause: Algorithm clarity over efficiency. Could use sorted vector or robin_hood_hashing.

real_issues.title: ImageCache Never Evicts — Unbounded Memory Growth
real_issues.description: LoadImage caches every loaded bitmap indefinitely in std::map<BString, BBitmap*>. Clear() only called on destruction. No LRU, no size limit, no weak refs.
real_issues.evidence: Line 42: `fCache[path] = bitmap;` Line 52-55: Clear deletes all. No eviction policy.
real_issues.impact: Long session with many inline images (Markdown renders) leaks GPU/texture memory. Haiku bitmap memory not tracked by malloc.
real_issues.root_cause: Cache designed for session lifetime, not bounded resource.

real_issues.title: SessionStore JSONL Parsing Allocates Per Line
real_issues.description: LoadSession reads JSONL line-by-line, calls json::Value::parse per line (which allocates parser, throws on error). No streaming/SAX parser. Message vectors reallocated per round.
real_issues.evidence: Line 138: `auto v = json::Value::parse(line);` inside while loop. parse() creates Parser object, uses exceptions.
real_issues.impact: Loading 1000-message session: ~200ms vs ~20ms with streaming parser. Memory fragmentation from many small allocations.
real_issues.root_cause: Reuses existing json::Value::parse designed for single documents, not logs.

hypothetical_findings.title: Provider Streaming Buffers Entire Response Before Callback
hypothetical_findings.description: StreamState accumulates full SSE chunks in buffer before parsing JSON and calling on_text. No incremental token delivery to UI. Large responses (8k+ tokens) delay first paint by 200-500ms.
hypothetical_findings.evidence: Anthropic.cpp:32 `buffer.append(data, size)`; Line 38 parses complete events. No callback until event complete.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: Perceived latency = TTFT + full chunk time. Streaming UX broken for long completions.

hypothetical_findings.title: Tool Results Not Truncated Before Context Insertion
hypothetical_findings.description: Tool outputs (bash, grep, glob, read_file) inserted verbatim into message history. A single `find / -name '*.cpp'` can emit 500KB. No cap_tool_output enforcement visible in Loop.cpp.
hypothetical_findings.evidence: Loop.h:112 declares `cap_tool_output` but Loop.cpp usage unclear. ToolRegistry.execute returns full output.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: Single tool call blows context window, triggers compaction, loses history. Token waste 10-100x.

hypothetical_findings.title: MCP Client Polls Stdio Transport Synchronously
hypothetical_findings.description: connect() likely blocks on readline from subprocess stdout. No async/overlapped I/O. Multiple MCP servers = sequential startup latency.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: 5 MCP servers × 2s startup = 10s GUI freeze on launch.

hypothetical_findings.title: Wiki Search Scores All Entries Linearly (No Inverted Index)
hypothetical_findings.description: WikiSearch iterates ALL g_wiki_entries, calls score_wiki_entry (tokenizes, builds sets) per entry. O(N) per query. No term→doc posting lists.
hypothetical_findings.evidence: Line 141: `for (const auto& entry : g_wiki_entries)` — full scan. Tokenize called per entry per query.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: 1000 wiki entries → 50ms/query. Scales poorly. TF-IDF precomputed but not indexed.

hypothetical_findings.title: Curl Easy Handles Recreated Per Request (No Pooling in Providers)
hypothetical_findings.description: Each CompletionRequest creates new CURL* via curl_easy_init, sets options, performs, cleans up. No connection reuse. TLS handshake per request adds 50-200ms.
hypothetical_findings.evidence: Provider.h:108 `CancelFlag*` but no persistent handle. Anthropic.cpp likely creates handle in send().
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: Streaming chat: new TLS handshake per turn. 10 turns = 1-2s wasted.

hypothetical_findings.title: TextDocumentLayout ParagraphLayout Re-shapes Glyphs on Every Invalidation
hypothetical_findings.description: _ValidateLayout calls ParagraphLayout::Layout which runs harfbuzz/icu shaping per paragraph. No glyph run cache. Identical paragraphs re-shaped after trivial edit elsewhere.
hypothetical_findings.evidence: TextDocumentLayout.cpp:200+ calls Layout per paragraph. ParagraphLayout likely owns shaping state.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: Typing in code file: 500 paragraphs × shaping = 50ms/frame. Explains PERF-001 root cause.

hypothetical_findings.title: SessionStore BFS Attribute Writes Sync per Message
hypothetical_findings.description: SaveSession calls write_string_attr/write_int64_attr per message for BFS metadata. Each WriteAttr is a syscall. 1000 messages = 4000 syscalls.
hypothetical_findings.evidence: Lines 68-110: attribute helpers. SaveSession likely calls per-message.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: Session save latency 50-100ms. Blocks UI thread.

hypothetical_findings.title: No Request Coalescing for Rapid Tool Calls
hypothetical_findings.description: Agent loop executes tools sequentially. If LLM emits 5 tool calls in one turn, each runs to completion before next. No parallelization of independent tools (read_file × 5).
hypothetical_findings.evidence: Loop.cpp RunTurn structure: single tool call per iteration typically.
hypothetical_findings.impact_if_true: 5 × 200ms file reads = 1s vs 200ms parallel. User-perceived latency 5x.

top_5_concerns.title: TextView Full Relayout on Every Keystroke
top_5_concerns.why: Directly blocks 60fps typing. User-facing latency. Core GUI differentiator. Fix unlocks large-file editing.

top_5_concerns.title: chars/4 Token Heuristic in Control Loops
top_5_concerns.why: Drives compaction, cost, context decisions. Wrong estimates = wasted tokens or overflow. Foundation for all token economics.

top_5_concerns.title: Provider Streaming Not Truly Incremental
top_5_concerns.why: Breaks streaming UX promise. First-token latency hidden but chunk latency visible. Easy win: parse SSE incrementally, callback per token.

top_5_concerns.title: SSE Handshake Allocation Storm
top_5_concerns.why: MCP startup on every launch. Fix is localized, zero-risk (string_view + reserve). Compounds with server count.

top_5_concerns.title: RAG/Wiki Linear Scan No Inverted Index
top_5_concerns.why: Knowledge retrieval is core differentiator. O(N) kills scaling. Inverted index is standard solution.
top_5_concerns.effort: Medium (build posting lists at index time)

architecture_smells.name: Global Mutable State for RAG/Wiki/Session
architecture_smells.description: g_entries, g_idf, g_wiki_entries, g_wiki_idf, dir_override() are global statics with mutex. Prevents multi-workspace, multi-tab isolation. Testing requires process isolation.
architecture_smells.risk: State leaks between tabs/workspaces. Concurrency bugs. Can't unit test without full init.

architecture_smells.name: UI-Agnostic Loop Coupled to Concrete Callbacks
architecture_smells.description: UiCallbacks is abstract but Loop.cpp assumes specific callback semantics (on_text streaming, on_tool_start/end). CLI, GUI, headless all implement differently. No formal contract.
architecture_smells.risk: Behavioral drift between UIs. New UI must reverse-engineer expectations. Hard to test Loop in isolation.

architecture_smells.name: Provider Abstraction Leaks Transport Details
architecture_smells.description: Provider.h exposes CancelFlag*, StreamEvent types tied to SSE. OpenAICompat handles reasoning models (o1/o3) with special logic in provider. Transport (curl) inside provider, not separate.
architecture_smells.risk: Adding new provider (Gemini, Vertex) requires copying curl+SSE logic. Can't swap HTTP client. Reasoning model logic duplicated.

architecture_smells.name: Tool Execution Synchronous, No Cancellation Granularity
architecture_smells.description: Tool::execute blocks until done. CancelFlag checked only at provider level, not inside tools. Long-running bash/glob can't be interrupted mid-execution.
architecture_smells.risk: User hits Ctrl+C — tool keeps running. Resource waste. No timeout enforcement per tool.

architecture_smells.name: Config Parsing Re-reads Files on Every Access
architecture_smells.description: ParseProviderConf opens/closes file, parses line-by-line per call. LoadConfig called at startup but providers may re-parse. No caching, no file watcher.
architecture_smells.risk: Negligible now but anti-pattern. Config changes require restart anyway (no hot-reload).

architecture_smells.name: Haiku-Specific Code Mixed with Portable Core
architecture_smells.description: #ifdef __HAIKU__ blocks throughout core modules. BFS attributes, live queries, node monitor in tools. Portable logic (JSONL, tokenization) tangled with platform API.
architecture_smells.risk: Hard to test on Linux CI. Platform bugs contaminate core. No clean abstraction layer for FS/query/attrs.

praise.title: System One Decision Model — Token Efficiency Masterstroke
praise.description: Delegating classification/verification/triage to local heuristic model (5-10x token savings) is architecturally brilliant. 9 focused tools replace verbose prompt chains. Persistent memory (remember/recall) enables learning. This alone justifies the project's existence.

praise.title: UI-Agnostic Agent Loop with Clean Callback Abstraction
praise.description: Loop.cpp shares 100% of agent logic between CLI, GUI, headless. UiCallbacks (on_text, on_tool_start, on_tool_end, on_error) is the right abstraction boundary. Enables rapid UI experimentation without touching core.

praise.title: BFS-Integrated Session Storage with Tracker Search
praise.description: Sessions as JSONL + BFS attributes (pluto:title, pluto:model, pluto:tags) makes history queryable in Tracker Find. No separate DB. Native Haiku feel. Atomic write (temp+rename) prevents corruption.

praise.title: Custom Text Layout Engine (Not WebView)
praise.description: TextDocumentLayout + ParagraphLayout + StreamingMarkdown = native Haiku text rendering. No Electron/CEF bloat. Supports code blocks, images, tool blocks, collapsible sections. 60fps scrolling achievable with incremental layout fix.

praise.title: MCP Transport Abstraction with SSRF Protection
praise.description: HttpTransport, SseTransport, StdioTransport share Transport interface. SseTransport.resolve_url validates origin to prevent SSRF. Manager handles project/user/local scopes with approval flow. Clean, secure, extensible.

praise.title: Auto-Compact at 90% with LLM Summarization
praise.description: Proactive context management: MaybeCompact triggers LLM summarization before overflow. Preserves recent turns, drops oldest. Manual /compact command. Token gauge in status bar. UX-forward thinking.

praise.title: Zero-Dependency JSON Parser (Correct & Auditable)
praise.description: json.cpp: 288 lines, no simdjson/nlohmann. Recursive descent with depth limit (256). Handles NaN/Inf. Serializable. Auditable for supply-chain security. Fast enough for config/session sizes.

praise.title: AsyncStreamManager — libcurl Multi Done Right
praise.description: Proper curl_multi usage: connection limits (MAXCONNECTS=10, MAX_HOST_CONNECTIONS=6), progress callback for cancellation, SSE parsing in write callback, drain loop. Handles concurrent provider streams cleanly.

veteran_quotes.author: Anonymous (18 years, compiler/runtime)

chars/4 token estimation in the hot path? That's not a heuristic, that's a bug waiting to be exploited. Integrate the provider's actual tokenizer or at least calibrate per-model. The compaction trigger will fire at wrong times and you'll lose context silently.
Anonymous (25 years, distributed systems)

System One is the kind of architecture I wish more LLM apps had: delegate cheap decisions to cheap models. 5-10x token savings on routing/guard/classification is real money. The persistent memory (remember/recall) turns it from stateless to stateful — that's the killer feature.
Anonymous (15 years, GUI frameworks)

Building a custom text layout engine on Haiku in 2025 is either insanity or brilliance. ParagraphLayout doing harfbuzz shaping per paragraph is correct. But caching glyph runs across invalidations is non-negotiable for 60fps. The ImageCache leak is amateur hour though — unbounded cache in a long-running app?
Anonymous (20 years, search/infra)

RAG and Wiki both doing linear scan with TF-IDF scoring? That's a prototype, not a product. Build an inverted index at ingestion time. Posting lists + BM25. 5000 docs should query in <1ms, not 50ms. The IDF rebuild on every dirty query is especially painful.
Anonymous (17 years, CLI/tooling)

GlobTool shelling out to `find` is the kind of pragmatism I respect — but it doesn't scale. Haiku's live queries (query_fs) are perfect for this. Wire it up and you get instant results + live updates. Same for grep — ripgrep exists, use it.
Anonymous (30 years, systems)

Global mutex-protected state for RAG/Wiki/Session? That's a single-workspace assumption baked into the architecture. When (not if) you add multi-tab or multi-workspace, you'll rewrite all three. Encapsulate behind a WorkspaceContext now.
Anonymous (19 years, networking)

SSE handshake parsing with string append/erase per chunk? That's allocation death by a thousand cuts. Use a ring buffer or string_view. The curl write callback gives you contiguous chunks — parse in place. 15ms saved per MCP connect adds up.
Anonymous (23 years, language runtimes)

JSON parser using exceptions for malformed input? LLM output is *frequently* malformed. You'll pay the exception unwind cost on every recovery. Switch to error codes or a non-throwing parser. The 256 recursion limit is also a stack overflow waiting to happen with nested tool calls.
Anonymous (16 years, build/release)

Four binaries sharing 40 compilation units via Makefile — clean, fast builds, no CMake bloat. The install.sh that handles Tracker add-on registration, resource files, and hpkg generation shows respect for the platform. Haiku devs will appreciate the native packaging.
